item.content:encoded:
Sure, and when I read one that does that and works for me, I'll upvote it! :)

Actually, I'm fairly sure that MrWrong's entry did.

A lot of the parody attempts in this contest (that I've seen) weren't well executed or even well conceived, in my opinion, though. Faking funny-because-it-is-terrible sort of misses the sincerity that makes "Eye of Argon" actually funny. I also think some of the authors in this contest perhaps felt that this was an excuse for low effort contributions, which don't appeal to me, even in these kind of events.

This does make me think a future contest done as a timed competition based on secret prompts might be actually kind of interesting (maybe with a slightly more sober presentation), probably with more warning but a shorter duration (maybe 45 minutes to an hour). I certainly would want to enter something like that (and I've competed in similar timed writing contests a few times). I do understand that wasn't actually the purpose of this contest, of course!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Disclaimer: I am inactive as staff right now. This is only my personal opinion.

"Making someone laugh" is legitimate artistic value. As one hears repeatedly in professional writing circles: Dying is easy. Comedy is hard.

This is great for April Fool's, but these articles are now part of the site proper forever

If there's anything wrong with that, it comes down to personal tastes. To many people (a great many people, by the looks of our reader base) it might instead be a breath of fresh air.

I would be perfectly happy for them to be under a "crackfic" tag, but seeing sloth pictures on the highest rated Tales of April 2016 seems like a retrograde step for the site.

Go look at Top Rated Pages. SCP-____-J is the second highest rated article on the site. The Things Dr Bright Is Not Allowed To Do At The Foundation is also near the top. On page two of Top Rated, you'll find Kill 682 (by the subject of the sloth pictures page, no less!).

It's true that these are not recent articles, but those sky-high ratings were created by the current population of the site.

Also: the sloth article currently stands at +0 (as does your other example) and is unusually low-content for the contest. Why worry about it at all?

A 'crackfic' tag is a good suggestion, though.

despite having been rated on essentially a different scale to normal, because of the context of the contest.

This remains to be seen. It's only been 48 hours. Even if people rated on a different scale (this remains to be seen as well), the contest is already over, and very few articles were voted on by more than a dozen people (…exactly a dozen are currently above +12, actually).

If people don't enjoy the articles for what they are, they will disappear. As always.

By normal site standards, I mean articles that, if they had been posted outside of this contest, would be in deletion range. That is based on my observation of site voting patterns

See Project Crossover (much of which would qualify for this contest), and stuff like The Death Of Alto Clef, Etc. If your observations were correct, these stories would have been deleted.

+ Collapsing the rest of this. Getting less coherent!
– hide block

I have avoided voting on any of the entries so far, because it seemed unfair to hold them to my standards (or normal standards generally) while the contest was running.

Fair enough, and this may be true for others as well, but the contest only lasted 48 hours and is already over.

The particular tale I referred to has no connection to the Foundationverse,

That's a weird gray area in our rules and wasn't a flaw in the contest (the author chose to forego using the character Neil R. Ghost, and instead used a literal fat ghost).

and has no literary purpose other than to titillate

The primary purpose could certainly be to amuse people who find that sort of thing amusing, actually. This covers entire genres of graphic sexual material.

This overall (not your specific post, psul) reminds me of a few minor dust-ups I've seen in the professional SFF world. Related tweet, the context of which is an award-nominated (but not -winning) April Fool's joke story: https://twitter.com/scalzi/status/715528678617313281

[PLZ NOTE: Not intended to direct profanity at psul's perfectly legit post.]

So in the Real World, people get unhappy about this sort of thing, too — but conflating 'seriousness' and 'quality'/'being legitimate' isn't considered an objective universal standard in the Real World either.

All that said, your personal tastes are perfectly legitimate. If you dislike this contest and This Sort Of Thing in general, that's fine.

Of the 20-odd pieces I've read so far, only two or three meet normal site standards,

This just isn't so, or if it is I'll be very surprised. As difficult as it is to get objective, consistent standards — our normal site standards are exceptionally low compared to The Real World. They're exceptionally high compared to other creepypasta / informal sites.

In terms of crackfic, there's lower standards with grammar and spelling, for example… but bluntly, most tales on this site are riddled with errors. They're just not errors that get noticed. Once you hit a certain quality bar, nobody notices if you go higher or not — something which has led to at least a small number of authors exiting this site once they've hit that bar and had no incentive to improve.

Many things that are considered very high-quality on this site would be considered painfully derivative (and not even in a good way) and badly written elsewhere, without enough intrinsic entertainment value outside this setting to pull off the "low quality but no one cares" Twilight strategy. This covers a very high number of SCPs and a significant subset of Tales.

(I could go on, but I really, really shouldn't. I apologize for any errors made here because I wrote this between 2AM and 3AM like an utter fool)

– hide block

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Clearly the popularity of the contest is such that I'm not going to kill its buzz. I do think that the dissenting opinion should be able to be shared. And despite all appearances, I don't object to the contest itself (even my initial concern about "celebrities" seems not to have been borne out too much, which is encouraging).

Happy April Fool's!

This is kinda my point. This is great for April Fool's, but these articles are now part of the site proper forever, despite having been rated on essentially a different scale to normal, because of the context of the contest. I would be perfectly happy for them to be under a "crackfic" tag, but seeing sloth pictures on the highest rated Tales of April 2016 seems like a retrograde step for the site.

Articles that are not within deletion range? Or the tales that are up to your standards? These are two inherently different categories.

By normal site standards, I mean articles that, if they had been posted outside of this contest, would be in deletion range. That is based on my observation of site voting patterns, not my personal standards. I have avoided voting on any of the entries so far, because it seemed unfair to hold them to my standards (or normal standards generally) while the contest was running.

There are tales which have scenes of explicit erotica, both in SCPs and tales (I'd be happy to provide a list if asked), which have not been taken down. This does apply to visual pornography.

The rules state that "no pornographic or excessively gory content is allowed". If this only applies to visual images, that should be clarified in the rules.

I understand that the line between erotica and pornography will be drawn differently by different people. The particular tale I referred to has no connection to the Foundationverse, consists entirely of a graphic sex scene, and has no literary purpose other than to titillate - there is no character, plot or theme. If that is not pornographic, then perhaps the site view is that text cannot ever constitute pornography.

Yes, roughly half of the entries are 0 or under, so most likely there'd be even more there would be in deletion range outside of the contest. People voting for contests are likely to be more lenient for them than not.

Is there a genuine suggestion from staff that a collection of photos of sloths, or of a cat, or "hilarious" misspellings, should form part of the Tales on the site for future members to read without context?

No, but that's up to the users to decide. This was an April Fool's thing we assumed that the userbase would enjoy (and indeed they did). And as evidenced from many forum comments and chat comments; there are a decent amount of tales that will be self-deleted that aren't in deletion range.

Also, there is at least one entry which is an item of pure pornography, which I thought was a breach of the rules. Why has the standard (summary) deletion policy not been applied in that case?

There are tales which have scenes of explicit erotica, both in SCPs and tales (I'd be happy to provide a list if asked), which have not been taken down. This does apply to visual pornography.
